'## Code to paste into ODC' section by `npm run embed:handover` (idempotent — re-run after
The project rule this serves: a handover ticket must CONTAIN the JS/CSS the developer pastes
into ODC — not just point at a repo path. A dev working inside ODC Studio cannot follow a link
into a repo they don't have open.
Entry shape — either a plain file list:
…or an object that also pins a fully-filled Mentor Studio prompt:
`mentor.kind` is one of: web-component | block | restyle. When `mentor` is omitted the prompt
is derived from the artifact kind automatically.
A handover with no code to embed (a screen walkthrough, say) still gets an entry: `"screen.md": []`.
Tokens are NOT listed here — they travel once via dist/theme.css, which is its own paste.
Add an entry for every new handover. A handover with no entry gets no embedded code, and the
embed silently goes stale when its source changes — so keep this in sync (check:state warns).

prompts.title: Prompt A — the reference Blocks (<<LSG_MODULE>>)
prompts.text:
Goal: In ODC Studio, create the Live Style Guide foundation Blocks for the <<DESIGN_SYSTEM_NAME>> design system. Each Block renders one kind of design token, read live from the theme.
Module: <<LSG_MODULE>>.

Context (already done manually — do NOT re-create or edit these):
- dist/theme.css is pasted into the theme of <<THEME_MODULE>>, which this module uses.
- lsg-token-reference.js is imported in this module as a Script named "LsgTokenReference". It defines the custom element <lsg-token-reference>.
- Do NOT write CSS, author or modify JavaScript, or edit the Theme.

Task — create these elements, referencing each by the exact name given:

1. Create one Block per foundation, in a UI Flow named "StyleGuideReferences":
   - "ColorReference": kind = "color"
   - "TypographyReference": kind = "font-size"
   - "FontWeightReference": kind = "font-weight"
   - "SpacingReference": kind = "space"
   - "RadiusReference": kind = "radius"
   - "BorderReference": kind = "border-size"
   - "ShadowReference": kind = "shadow"
2. Give every Block the same three Text inputs: Heading, Intro and Filter (all optional, default "").
3. In each Block, add one HTML Element widget with Tag = "lsg-token-reference" and these attributes (the platform requires an expression on every attribute):
     kind    = the literal for that Block from step 1, e.g. "color"
     heading = Heading
     intro   = Intro
     filter  = Filter
   Nothing else goes inside the Block.
4. Set each Block's Required Scripts to the one Script "LsgTokenReference". Do not load it any other way.

OutSystems UI rules to follow: never edit the OutSystems UI module; never paste HTML into an Expression; keep each Block to the single HTML Element above.

After generating, list every Block you created with its HTML Element attributes, and flag anything you could not finish.
Start with ColorReference and show it to me before creating the others.

prompts.title: Prompt B — the Styles screens (<<LSG_MODULE>>)
prompts.text:
Goal: In ODC Studio, put the foundation Blocks on the Styles screens of the Live Style Guide for the <<DESIGN_SYSTEM_NAME>> design system.
Module: <<LSG_MODULE>>.

Context: the Blocks ColorReference, TypographyReference, FontWeightReference, SpacingReference, RadiusReference, BorderReference and ShadowReference already exist in this module (previous prompt). Do NOT edit them, and do NOT write CSS or JavaScript.

Task:
1. On each Styles screen, inside the layout's MainContent placeholder, place the matching Block: the Colors screen gets ColorReference, the Typography screen TypographyReference followed by FontWeightReference, and Spacing, Border radius, Border size and Shadow their own Block. If a screen does not exist yet, create it in the same flow as the other Styles screens, on the module's default layout, and add it to the menu the same way the existing Styles screens are.
2. Set each Block's Intro to the one-sentence intro already on that screen, if there is one. Remove any hand-built swatch, scale or table on the screen that the Block now renders: the Block replaces it.
3. Leave the brand narrative on the Colors screen where it is, above the Block.

After generating, list each screen and the Block placed on it, and every widget you removed.
